tasks.title: Add the audit round reader
tasks.acceptance:
- A reader for recorded audit rounds implements §2.1's five definitions: the trimmed non-empty role predicate (never case-folded, reserved regression id not special-cased), the byte-exact PASS predicate matching the record path, and the four contributes-no-rows causes (empty file entry, unreadable file, a non-blank line that does not unmarshal into a JSON map, an empty or differing stored roles_hash).
- Each no-rows round emits exactly one output.Notice from §2.1's five-row advisory table, chosen by the fixed evaluation order: the hash test first with its empty case before its differing case, then the three file-based causes in table order. engine.LoadRoundRows and its existing callers are unchanged.
- Tests 5, 6, 7, 8, 9 and 11 pass, including the discriminating halves: a bare null line is a row, a trailing newline is not a parse failure, and the corpus wording wins over the missing-file wording on a round to which both apply.
tasks.closed_reason:
- internal/engine/auditrounds.go implements §2.1's five definitions: AuditRowRole trims the role string and drops empty/whitespace-only/non-string values without ever case-folding (so "Spec-Coverage" stays a distinct id) and does not special-case the reserved regression id; AuditRowIsPass is byte-for-byte cli.countAuditFindings' status != PASS test; ReadAuditRoundRows implements the four contributes-no-rows causes (empty file entry, unreadable file, a non-blank line that does not unmarshal into a JSON map, an empty or differing stored roles_hash).
- Each no-rows round emits exactly one output.Notice from the five-row advisory table in the fixed evaluation order — empty stored hash, differing stored hash, empty file entry, unreadable file, unparseable line — verified in internal/engine/auditrounds_test.go by asserting captured stderr equals the expected wording exactly (one line, no second advisory), plus a multi-bad-line fixture that still costs one advisory.
- engine.LoadRoundRows and its existing callers are unchanged: no file outside internal/engine/auditrounds.go and its test was touched, and the test asserts LoadRoundRows still reports the same not-found for an empty file entry and for a missing file, which is why §2 needs its own reader.
- Tests 5, 6, 7, 8, 9 and 11 pass in internal/engine/auditrounds_test.go, including the discriminating halves: a bare null line is a row carrying no role and non-PASS while 5, "x", true and [] each make the round contribute no rows; a trailing newline, a blank line, a whitespace-only line and CRLF endings all contribute rows with no advisory; and the corpus wording wins over the missing-file wording on a round that both differs in hash and has no file on disk. Six mutations (case-fold role, trim status, drop the blank-line skip, require a JSON object, read the file before the hash test, let an empty stored hash match an empty latest hash) each failed a named assertion and were reverted. Gate: go test ./... exit 0, golangci-lint run exit 0.

tasks.title: Compute per-role clean streaks
tasks.acceptance:
- role_streaks carries one entry per role in the latest recorded round as {role, consecutive_clean, open}, spec-coverage first and the rest ascending by byte order, and is an emitted empty array — never null, never omitted — whenever no role appears there.
- The walk starts at the latest round and stops when every latest-round role's streak is closed, when a round contributes no rows, or at the start of history, so the §2.1 advisory can fire at most once per invocation.
- Tests 1, 2, 3, 4, 12, 13, 16 and 17 pass, including that a round absent a role ends that role's streak rather than being skipped, and that a corpus change between recorded rounds truncates the streak.
tasks.closed_reason:
- internal/engine/rolestreaks.go adds engine.ComputeAuditRoleStreaks, returning one RoleStreak{role, consecutive_clean, open} per role of the latest recorded audit round, spec-coverage first (engine.RoleSpecCoverage) and the rest ascending by plain Go byte comparison, from a slice made with make so it emits as [] and never null; TestComputeAuditRoleStreaks_PerRoleStreaks pins the entry shape against the marshalled JSON and TestComputeAuditRoleStreaks_EmptyArrayStates asserts json.Marshal returns "[]" in all six no-role states.
- The walk starts at the latest round and its loop condition is i >= 0 && len(streakOpen) > 0, so it stops when every latest-round streak has closed, breaks on the first round ReadAuditRoundRows reports as contributing no rows, and ends at the start of history; TestComputeAuditRoleStreaks_WalkStopsAtAStreakClosingRound asserts no advisory at all is emitted over a five-round fixture whose round 2 file is deleted below the round that closes every streak, and the corpus-change and empty-hash tests assert the advisory names exactly the round the walk stopped on.
- Tests 1, 2, 3, 4, 12, 13, 16 and 17 pass in internal/engine/rolestreaks_test.go, including that a round absent a role ends that role's streak (round 2 measuring only another role gives 1, not 3) and that a corpus change between recorded rounds truncates it (four all-PASS rounds split old/old/new/new give 2, not 4, with the second half asserting an earlier empty stored hash emits the has-no-auditor-corpus-hash wording rather than the different-corpus one). Verified by mutation: skipping unmeasured rounds fails test 2 only, a case-insensitive sort fails test 4 only, dropping the streak-closed loop guard fails test 16 only, and a nil slice fails test 17 only.
- Halves belonging to dependent tasks, not claimed here: test 12's and test 13's spec_coverage_clean_rounds assertions (2 and null) are spec-coverage-field's, asserted here as the spec-coverage entry's consecutive_clean and as the empty array; test 17's raw-JSON assertion on the emitted payload is audit-output-wiring's, approximated here by marshalling the returned slice.
- Out of scope: ComputeAuditRoleStreaks also returns the latest round's rows so divergence-object can count roleless open rows without a second ReadAuditRoundRows call over the same entry, which would re-parse the file and could re-fire the section 2.1 advisory this walk fires at most once; nothing consumes that return value yet.

tasks.title: Report spec-coverage streak by name
tasks.acceptance:
- spec_coverage_clean_rounds carries the spec-coverage role's consecutive_clean, or an explicit JSON null when the latest recorded round contributes no row attributed to that id, in §2.1's sense of contributes.
- The key is always emitted, including when its value is null and including under --compact; null and 0 are never collapsed.
- Test 18 passes, with its discriminating half: null when the latest round holds no spec-coverage row even though an earlier round does.
tasks.closed_reason:
- engine.SpecCoverageCleanRounds in internal/engine/speccoverage.go returns the spec-coverage entry's consecutive_clean as a *int, or nil when the latest recorded round contributes no row attributed to that id: it reads the role_streaks ComputeAuditRoleStreaks already returned, whose entries are exactly the roles of the latest round in §2.1's sense of contributes, so a readable round with an empty stored roles_hash yields no entries and therefore nil without a second read (or a re-fired advisory).
- The *int return keeps null and 0 distinct at the JSON boundary and lets a caller emit the key without omitempty; TestSpecCoverageCleanRounds_NullAndZeroDoNotCollapse marshals both through a field with no omitempty and asserts the key is present and the two renderings differ. Wiring the field into the --status/--record payload, including under --compact, belongs to audit-output-wiring.
- Test 18 is covered by both halves: TestSpecCoverageCleanRounds_NullWhenOnlyAnEarlierRoundHoldsTheRole (the discriminating half — null when only an earlier round holds the role) and TestSpecCoverageCleanRounds_ZeroWhenTheLatestRoundHoldsAnOpenRow (0 when the latest round holds a non-PASS spec-coverage row). TestSpecCoverageCleanRounds_NullStates adds the remaining no-attributed-row states (no recorded round, deleted file, empty file entry, unparseable line, zero rows, all rows roleless, a differently-cased id), and TestSpecCoverageCleanRounds_ReturnsACopy pins that the pointer cannot mutate the streaks array.
- Test 12's and test 13's spec_coverage_clean_rounds halves, left open by role-streaks, are covered here: CorpusChangeBetweenRoundsTruncatesTheNumber (2, not 4), EmptyStoredHashOnAnEarlierRoundTruncatesTheNumber (2), and NullWhenTheLatestRoundHasAnEmptyStoredHash (null). Their role_streaks halves are already asserted in rolestreaks_test.go; test 17's role_streaks half likewise stays there, and every CLI-payload half of tests 17 and 29 belongs to audit-output-wiring.
- Verified by mutation: returning &0 instead of nil makes NullWhenOnlyAnEarlierRoundHoldsTheRole, NullWhenTheLatestRoundHasAnEmptyStoredHash and every NullStates subtest fail, and skipping the entry when consecutive_clean is 0 makes ZeroWhenTheLatestRoundHoldsAnOpenRow fail; both reverted. Gate green with separate exit codes: go test ./... = 0, golangci-lint run = 0.

tasks.title: Build the divergence object
tasks.acceptance:
- divergence is emitted only when all five §2.4 conditions hold, and is an omitted key rather than null otherwise; condition 5 is plain equality between the latest round's stored roles_hash and the corpus hash computed now, and constrains --status alone.
- Its five fields are always present when the object is emitted: other_roles_open, open_roles (each id once, ascending, [] when every open row is unattributed), unattributed_open (0 rather than absent), message in one of the three §2.4 forms with the counts taken from spec_coverage_clean_rounds and other_roles_open, and hint equal to the §2.6 constant verbatim.
- Tests 14, 15, 19, 20, 21, 22, 23, 24, 25 and 26 pass, including that condition 4 withholds the object at a resolved audit_clean_rounds of 0 and that an unreadable corpus withholds it by both routes.
tasks.closed_reason:
- engine.ComputeAuditDivergence (internal/engine/divergence.go) emits the divergence object only when all five §2.4 conditions hold and returns nil — an omitted key, never a JSON null — otherwise; condition 5 is plain equality between the latest recorded round's stored roles_hash and the corpus hash computed now, which is why it constrains --status alone (on --record the caller passes the hash it stamped on the just-recorded round, so the equality holds by construction), and condition 4 keeps the object from being emitted beside an already-open gate at a resolved audit_clean_rounds of 0.
- All five fields are always present in an emitted object: other_roles_open counts every non-PASS row not attributed to spec-coverage, open_roles names those roles once each in ascending byte order and is an emitted [] when every open row is unattributed, unattributed_open is 0 rather than absent, message is one of the three §2.4 forms with the round count taken from spec_coverage_clean_rounds and the finding count from other_roles_open (only those two nouns inflect), and hint is the §2.6 constant exported as engine.DivergenceHint.
- internal/engine/divergence_test.go covers tests 19, 20, 21, 22, 23, 26 and the engine halves of 14, 15, 24 and 25 over fixtures that write a real auditor corpus and derive every condition input through the helpers the audit outputs call (SpecHash, ComputeRolesHash, ComputeAuditRoleStreaks, SpecCoverageCleanRounds, StateStale, Converged), so a state the resolver cannot produce cannot be asserted; test 15's route 2 makes the corpus genuinely unreadable with a dangling symlink rather than a permission bit. 18 mutations were applied one at a time and every one killed its named test: each of the five conditions, each of the three message forms, the round and finding slots, the plural rule, the spec-coverage exclusion, the open_roles sort, dedup and nil-slice shape, and the hint constant.
- Test halves belonging to audit-output-wiring, not claimed here: test 14's assertion that roles_stale reads true on the tp audit --status payload (asserted here through engine.RolesStale over the same state, not through the CLI output) and test 24's assertion that tp audit --status --check exits 0 on the threshold-0 fixture. Test 22's 'an implementation emitting "divergence": null fails' is pinned here only against a payload map assembled the way a caller assembles one; the emitted CLI payload is wiring's.
- Gate: go test ./... exit 0, golangci-lint run exit 0 (checked with separate exit codes, not a && chain).

tasks.title: Emit the signal on both audit outputs
tasks.acceptance:
- spec_coverage_clean_rounds, role_streaks and divergence appear on tp audit <spec> --status with or without --check, and on tp audit <spec> --record <file> computed after the round is stored; they appear nowhere else, including tp audit --merge, tp audit <spec> prompt emission and every tp review mode.
- --compact keeps all three whole, including divergence.message and divergence.hint and the null-valued spec_coverage_clean_rounds key; the audit fields --compact already drops are unchanged.
- Tests 10, 27, 28, 29 and 31 pass, including that --check carries the same payload it carries without the flag.
tasks.closed_reason:
- internal/cli/audit_record.go wires role_streaks, spec_coverage_clean_rounds and divergence onto both outputs through one shared auditSignalFields helper: runAuditStatus calls it before the --check exit-code branch, so --status carries the three fields with or without --check, and runAuditRecord calls it after recordAuditRoundEntry has stored the round, so the latest recorded round is the round just recorded; recordAuditRoundEntry now returns the auditor-corpus hash it stamped and --record passes that value back as condition 5's right-hand side, so the equality holds by construction there and condition 5 constrains --status alone. engine.Converged, engine.ConsecutiveClean, the stored per-round clean flag and AuditNextAction are untouched, and the budget-refusal path still exits 4 before any payload.
- auditSignalFields is called from exactly those two sites and from nowhere else, so tp audit --merge, tp audit <spec> prompt emission and every tp review mode emit none of the three; TestAuditSignal_AbsentFromEveryOtherOutput asserts the absence of all three key names on tp audit <spec> --affected-files, tp audit --merge -o, tp review <spec> --record and tp review <spec> --status.
- The three fields are written outside both !IsCompact() guards, so --compact keeps role_streaks whole, keeps every field of divergence with message and hint byte-identical to their non-compact values, and keeps the spec_coverage_clean_rounds key when its value is null (a typed nil *int marshals as an emitted JSON null, never an absent key); TestAuditSignal_CompactKeepsAllThreeWhole compares the three fields field-by-field between compact and non-compact runs of both --status and --record, on a diverging fixture and on a separate null-valued fixture.
- The audit fields --compact already drops are unchanged: harness_stale, harness_note and overlap_report stay inside their existing !IsCompact() guards on both paths, and the same test asserts harness_stale is absent from the compact --record payload and both harness_stale and overlap_report from the compact --status payload.
- internal/cli/audit_signal_test.go lands tests 10, 27, 28, 29 and 31 plus the CLI halves of 14, 17, 22 and 24: test 10 asserts the missing-file advisory on both --status and --record over one fixture; 27 asserts --record emits divergence in the same invocation that completes the streak; 28 asserts --status --check carries all three, exits 1, and matches the payload --status carries without the flag field-by-field; 29 is the compact comparison above; 31 is the absence sweep above; 14 pins that a corpus edited after the latest round leaves the streaks intact, reads roles_stale true and withholds divergence; 17 pins raw-JSON "role_streaks": [] and "spec_coverage_clean_rounds": null over three empty states; 22 pins divergence as an omitted key rather than a null; 24 pins that a task-file audit_clean_rounds of 0 reaching the resolver leaves the gate open, so condition 4 withholds the object and --status --check exits 0. Verified by mutation: guarding the --status call on !check fails tests 28 and 24; moving the two fields inside if !IsCompact() fails test 29; computing the --record signal over the pre-record rounds fails tests 27, 10, 14, 22 and 24; feeding --status the latest round's stored roles_hash instead of the freshly computed one fails test 14. Gate run with separate exit codes: go test ./... exited 0 and golangci-lint run exited 0.

tasks.title: Guard the untouched convergence gate
tasks.acceptance:
- A guard test asserts that a fixture whose latest round holds only non-spec-coverage findings still reports clean false and converged false, that tp audit --status --check still exits 1, and that next_action is still the fix-and-re-audit directive on the same invocation that emits divergence.
- engine.Converged, engine.ConsecutiveClean, the stored per-round clean flag, AuditNextAction and tp resume are unchanged, and the test fails any implementation that lets the divergence signal reach convergence arithmetic or the next_action precedence.
- Test 30 passes.

tasks.title: Define the mechanized class predicate
tasks.acceptance:
- An entry is valid when engine.ValidateChecks accepts it on its own, judged per entry and never over the slice, so one invalid entry never changes another entry's treatment and a class named by two entries is simply registered.
- A class is mechanized when a valid entry's class equals it byte-for-byte, with no trimming and no case folding; over-specification is exempt from the reviewer exclusion list only, and is mechanized for candidate suppression like any other class.
- Tests 34, 35 and 36 pass, including that a slice-level validation suppresses neither class and fails.
source_sections: ## 3. A registered check retires its mechanize candidate
tasks.closed_reason:
- engine.IsMechanizedClass and engine.ReviewerExclusionClasses in internal/engine/mechanized.go judge validity per entry through the unexported checkIsValid, which calls engine.ValidateChecks on a one-element slice — the same single-entry call runMechanicalChecks makes — so one rejected entry never changes another entry's class and the cross-entry duplicate-class rule is unreachable, leaving a class named by two entries simply registered and named once in the exclusion list.
- The class comparison is plain == against the entry's class: no trimming, no case folding, so a reviewer-written "Duplicate-Line" or " duplicate-line " is not mechanized by a registered duplicate-line entry.
- over-specification is mechanized like any other class in IsMechanizedClass (the candidate-suppression sink) and is dropped from ReviewerExclusionClasses alone, after invalid entries are dropped and before duplicates collapse, so the prompt cannot both demand and forbid the class.
- internal/engine/mechanized_test.go covers the predicate halves of tests 34, 35 and 36 plus the §3.2 filter order and non-nil shape; verified by mutation: whole-slice validation fails the per-entry and two-entry tests, EqualFold+TrimSpace fails the exactness test, exempting over-specification in IsMechanizedClass fails the scoped-exemption test, and collapsing duplicates before dropping invalid entries fails the filter-order test. Gate green: go test ./... exit 0, golangci-lint run exit 0.
Out of scope: the end-to-end halves of tests 34-36 assert mechanize_candidates, mechanized_classes and both prompt-emission sites, which are the sinks owned by candidate-suppression, exclusion-list and mechanized-classes-field; this task ships the predicate they consume.

tasks.title: Suppress mechanized classes from candidates
tasks.acceptance:
- tp review <spec> --record filters mechanize_candidates, the register-a-check hint and the class list handed to next_action; tp review <spec> --status filters the class list handed to next_action through its own separate call over the recorded rounds.
- The frequency threshold is unchanged and suppressing one class never changes whether another crosses it; the filtered mechanize_candidates stays an emitted array and never becomes null.
- Tests 32, 33, 38, 39, 40 and 45 pass, including that tp review --report still lists a registered class and that the varying side of the exactness test is the finding row's class.

tasks.title: Filter the reviewer exclusion list
tasks.acceptance:
- The Mechanically checked classes list takes three membership changes in order — drop invalid entries, drop over-specification, then collapse duplicates keeping the first survivor — and keeps registration order otherwise; when the result is empty the sentence is not appended at all.
- Both assembly sites change: the multi-role panel in internal/cli/review.go and the tp review <spec> --perspective regression path in internal/cli/review_regression.go. The surrounding checks-running branch and the panel path's review_loop instruction addendum keep their own guards.
- Tests 37, 42, 43 and 44 pass, with the all-invalid case asserted through each entry's skipping invalid check notice over a fixture that resolves a task file.

tasks.title: Emit the mechanized classes field
tasks.acceptance:
- mechanized_classes is emitted on tp review <spec> --record and nowhere else, carrying the withheld candidate classes each once and sorted ascending, and survives --compact alongside mechanize_candidates.
- It is always an array on that output — [] when nothing was withheld, never an omitted key and never null — and it never lists a registered class that failed to reach candidate frequency.
- Test 41 passes, with the null half as its discriminating assertion.

- Both describe the three new audit fields and the suppression rule accurately enough for a driver to act on them without reading the spec.
